# TrustedQSL .tq5 fixtures

Generated by `tqsl_createCertRequest` from Debian `trustedqsl` **2.8.7-1**,
configuration 11.35, on amd64. `new.tq5` and `additional.tq5` are unmodified
outputs. The latter was signed by a randomly generated disposable test key;
`signer.pem` is its locally issued public test certificate. It is not an ARRL
certificate. The private key is not stored in the repository.

Run `sh testdata/tq5/generate.sh EMPTY_OUTPUT_DIRECTORY`. The container build
uses the signed Debian snapshot dated **2026-11-24 00:00 UTC**, with package
and matching source pinned to 2.8.7-1. The checked-in fixtures were originally
generated from the same package version on sid before the snapshot pin was
added; they were not replaced when the pinned generator was verified. Generation runs
with networking disabled, a fresh temporary TQSL store, and a newly generated
test CA and signer. Outputs contain random keys and timestamps and will not be
byte-identical between runs. Inspect regenerated output before replacing any
fixtures; do not change a fixture to make a failing test pass.

Tests compare the complete output bytes, replacing only CSR and signature
values while retaining their headers and lengths. They also compare CSR subject
and algorithm, verify the TrustedQSL signature using the fixture certificate,
and compare the library's signature with RSA PKCS#1 v1.5 over its request DER.
CSR keys and signatures differ because TQSL and the library generate fresh keys.

To verify freshly generated output without replacing the checked-in fixtures:

```
GABBI_TQ5_FIXTURE_DIR=EMPTY_OUTPUT_DIRECTORY CGO_ENABLED=0 go test -run TestBuildRequestTrustedQSLGolden -count=1
```
